# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

<!-- cap-evolve:insights-append-below -->

## The runtime bypasses `orchestrator.md` for most tasks (STRUCTURAL FACT, not a hypothesis)
- What worked: nothing confirmed by a RESULT yet (cand_0001 is unscored as I write).
- **Verified fact, independent of any gate result** (read directly from the runtime
  source, then confirmed by executing the classifier over all 67 instructions):
  `classify_fast()` in `_run/parsec-live/src/agent/agents.py:256` is a regex
  classifier run BEFORE the orchestrator LLM. On a match,
  `orchestrator.py:1202` dispatches the sub-agent and `return`s, so
  `orchestrator.md` is never constructed. **53 of 67 val tasks are fast-pathed;
  only 14 read `orchestrator.md`.** 10 of the 11 worst-scoring tasks are
  fast-pathed.
  - Consequence for every future iteration: **`shared_context.md` + the domain
    files are the real edit surface.** Budget spent on `orchestrator.md` can only
    reach 14 tasks. Verify routing with the classifier before attributing any
    failure to orchestrator routing.
- Promising but not yet tried: splitting `shared_context.md`'s rules down into the
  domain files, keeping only genuinely domain-general ones shared. Worth testing if
  cand_0001 is rejected without a clear per-task cause (dilution hypothesis).

## A chunk of the lost score is a CAPABILITY-GAP that prose cannot reach
- Verified fact: for ~6 tasks (~3.4 task-points, the single largest cluster) the
  fast-path hands the request to a sub-agent that has **no tool** for the data
  source the task needs, and sub-agents cannot hand off. The agent then substitutes
  another source or says the data is unavailable. Examples of the *shape* (not a
  task list to memorise): a marketplace-inventory question routed to the cost agent
  by the word "budget"; an Icinga question routed to babylon because the service
  name contains "Babylon"; a cost question needing a job record routed to the cost
  agent, which has no AAP2 tool.
- What didn't: no prompt rule can recover these — the required facts live behind a
  tool the agent does not have. Do not spend an iteration on them.
- Promising: fixing it needs code (priority-ordered patterns, fall through to the
  orchestrator on multi-domain matches, or allow handoff). See
  FRAMEWORK_IMPROVEMENTS.md.

## "Flaky" in the brief conflates two very different things
- Verified fact: of the 48 tasks listed as flaky, many have **zero variance** across
  10 trials at a fixed sub-1.0 value (e.g. 0.383, 0.500, 0.600 in all ten). Those are
  systematic, fully-diagnosable misses — usually one unmatched expected call or one
  always-missed rubric item — and are the cheapest real gains available. Separate
  them from true trial-to-trial variance before ranking clusters.

## The baseline prompt was itself the cause of three clusters
- Verified fact: three baseline sentences stated something false about a tool and
  directly produced 9–10/10-trial failures — "Always use `get_job_log` instead of
  `get_job`" (the graded call is `get_job`), "fetch_github_file — Fetch files and
  directories" (a directory path errors), and "`search_aap2_logs` with the controller
  hostname … in `cluster_host_id`" (the seeded rows carry the short name).
- Lesson for future iterations: **before adding prose, grep the prompt for a rule
  that already forbids the graded behaviour.** A deletion or correction is a
  higher-confidence edit than any addition, and no amount of added text overrides a
  standing "ALWAYS do X" instruction.
